Date: 2025-08-05 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Ellis (Arbiter - Head ML), Priya Nair (CTO), Ethan Cole (Cloud Eng)
summary: Renewal check-in focused on upgrading reserved capacity and activating geocluster (EU + APAC). Customer evaluating 12 vs 24 month extension, latency SLOs for customer-facing models, and private VPC activation for compliance. Action: send pricing, plan pilot benchmarks, share security docs and KMS flow.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining—quick audio check?
[00:07] Jordan (Arbiter): Yep hear you, all good.
[00:12] Maya (Redwood): Awesome. We'll run through renewal numbers, geocluster activation steps and then open for Qs.
[00:21] Priya (Arbiter): High level — we want to lock in committed capacity and push EU+APAC activation before holiday ramp. Also need to validate privacy/KMS flow.
[00:34] Samir (Redwood): Totally. Last term you were on 8 units dedicated, we showed a capacity model that maps to peak token throughput. For the renewal we're proposing a 40% uplift for seasonal headroom; option A is 12-month, option B is 24-month with discount.
[00:52] Jordan (Arbiter): Can you walk the math again, like how that 40% maps to p50/p95 and burst behavior? We had some unexpected queueing on the last Black Friday-ish test.
[01:04] Maya (Redwood): Sure, so baseline is average payload 450 tokens, model variant rdx-3b-opt. At 8 units you saw p50 ~ 80 ms, p95 ~ 350 ms in our hosted traces; the burst window depends on continuous batching and autoscale thresholds. If we add the 40% to reserved, burst capacity reduces queueing and your p95 drops toward ~220 ms in our sim. There's noise because of seq length and KV cache warm up.
[01:30] Ethan (Arbiter): Quick Q — are those numbers from our prod model or the samplebench? I remember different perf on our longer prompts.
[01:36] Maya (Redwood): It's hybrid; we ran your samplebench traces plus a small replay of production; longer prompts increase per-token compute and change batch shapes so p95 can drift. We'll share the perf profile we used.
[01:46] Priya (Arbiter): On the governance side — we need VPC private deployment plus KMS integration, SOC2 audit logs, and SSO. Any blockers?
[01:54] Samir (Redwood): All supported. VPC peering and private control plane for Private customers. KMS/HSM integration is available — we do customer-managed keys via the KMS shim, and audit logs stream to your SIEM. For SOC2 we have latest attestation and a security packet I'll attach.
[02:10] Jordan (Arbiter): Are there any caveats around cold KV cache when we switch variants? Last time we saw a cold-slow for a particular endpoint after fallback.
[02:19] Maya (Redwood): Good point — fallback across model variants can cause cold-cache misses. Our recommended pattern: pin critical endpoints to a primary variant and enable a warm-standby variant with lightweight KV pre-warm. We can automate pre-warm during canary rollouts.
[02:34] Ethan (Arbiter): About geocluster activation — what lead time do you need to have EU and APAC regions fully provisioned? We have compliance windows in September.
[02:42] Samir (Redwood): For Hosted + Dedicated hybrid we typically need 3 weeks to provision and validate EU geocluster and about 4-5 weeks for APAC depending on GPU availability and legal onboarding. For Private (VPC/on-prem) it's more dependent on your infra readiness — but target 6 weeks end-to-end if you're doing KMS/HSM and network approvals.
[03:00] Priya (Arbiter): Hmm that's tight. Could we stage EU first and then APAC after initial ramp?
[03:05] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely, staggered activation is common — EU first as priority, APAC as follow-up. We recommend finalizing term and committed units so we can reserve capacity.
[03:15] Jordan (Arbiter): On pricing — what does the uplift look like for 12 vs 24 months? Anything that requires capital P purchase of dedicated nodes?
[03:22] Samir (Redwood): We have two paths: reserved capacity (monthly commit) or dedicated pools (reserved GPUs). 24-month term gives you deeper discount on monthly commit and priority provisioning windows. We can show a blended TCO comparison with estimated token cost at current utilization profiles.
[03:37] Priya (Arbiter): Is there an SLA delta between committed reserved and dedicated?
[03:41] Maya (Redwood): Dedicated includes uptime SLA and prioritized capacity during incidents; reserved commit has SLAs around maintenance windows but lower priority during large-scale cloud events.
[03:50] Ethan (Arbiter): Security: we need proof flows for KMS wrap/unwrap — how keys are used in inference path, and whether tokens or caches ever leave our KMS boundary.
[03:58] Maya (Redwood): Keys are used to encrypt model artifacts and transport keys for ephemeral caches. The KV cache stays within the serving runtime and we can document flow; nothing leaves without being encrypted with your customer-managed key. We'll include architecture diagram in the security pack.
[04:15] Jordan (Arbiter): Great. Also are you able to run a performance benchmark inside our VPC using our synthetic traces? We want to replicate p95 under controlled network.
[04:24] Samir (Redwood): Yes — we run pilot benchmarks in-customer VPCs. We'll need access to a staging env, peering or a bastion, and your representative traces. That is one of the items in the next steps.
[04:34] Priya (Arbiter): About billing — we may need a PO routed through our procurement with a slightly different invoicing cadence. Any flex?
[04:41] Samir (Redwood): We support various billing cadences and can route invoices to procurement. For enterprise customers we can do quarterly invoice schedules or net-30/60 terms with the contract amendment.
[04:52] Jordan (Arbiter): One more — competitor question. We ran a quick eval of ApexInference and NimbusOps. Apex had lower latency for smaller context, Nimbus had cheaper pre-quantized instances. Why Redwood again?
[05:03] Maya (Redwood): A couple of callouts: we focus on unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private with predictable ops controls — so you get same API/rollouts everywhere. Our caching + batch policies are tuned for production to lower token cost without sacrificing latency. Also we provide the rollout/traceability features for audits.
[05:22] Ethan (Arbiter): Ok we like that, but we need concrete numbers in the renewal paperwork.
[05:26] Samir (Redwood): We'll include a TCO sheet with projected token/unit pricing, and a sample SLA appendix for dedicated vs reserved.
[05:33] Priya (Arbiter): Can you include an explicit clause about data residency when geocluster is active? We need that for procurement.
[05:40] Samir (Redwood): Yes — data residency clauses and contractual commitments for region-bound processing can be added. I'll loop legal if needed.
[05:47] Jordan (Arbiter): Timeline check: if we sign by Aug 18, can we get EU live by Sep 10?
[05:53] Maya (Redwood): Close but possible — with reserved capacity and prioritized provisioning we can push EU ~3 weeks post-sign. So signing by Aug 18 -> EU by Sep 8-10 is achievable assuming no red tape on peering and KMS. APAC would follow ~4-5 weeks after equipment allocation.
[06:08] Priya (Arbiter): Sounds good. Last administrative — can you share SOC2 packet and your current penetration test summary?
[06:15] Samir (Redwood): Yes, security pack will include SOC2, penetration test summary (redacted), architecture diagrams, and KMS flow.
[06:22] Jordan (Arbiter): OK let's talk about pilot scope — we want to run two endpoints: customer-facing chat and internal reranker. Different latency profiles.
[06:30] Maya (Redwood): For chat we'll optimize for p50; for reranker we can tune batching for throughput. We'll bring recommended quantization profiles — you may accept a small quality delta for 2-4x cost improvement.
[06:42] Ethan (Arbiter): Do you have A/B rollback built in if quality regresses post-quantization?
[06:47] Maya (Redwood): Yes — canary + automatic fallback to higher precision model if quality drops beyond threshold tied to eval prompts. We support prompt-set tied regressions and alerts.
[06:57] Samir (Redwood): Ok recap: Samir sends pricing + contract amendment and data residency clause; Maya sends perf profiles and batching/quant suggestion; Arbiter provides network/KMS details and representative traces; schedule pilot benchmark for week of Aug 13–15.
[07:10] Priya (Arbiter): Thanks all, this was useful.
[07:13] Samir (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.
[07:18] Jordan (Arbiter): Bye.
notes_topics: Topics covered: renewal terms (12 vs 24 mo), reserved vs dedicated capacity, geocluster activation (EU/APAC), VPC/KMS integration, SOC2/security docs, pilot benchmarking, pricing/TCO, staging timeline, billing cadence and procurement needs.
final_recap: Samir: Send pricing and contract amendment; Maya: share perf and quantization suggestions; Arbiter: provide traces, VPC/KMS metadata; target pilot benchmark 2025-08-13 to 08-15; EU activation target early Sept if signed by Aug 18.
